Container.Name: yes-captain
Container.Overview: Yes, Captain! A bridge simulator for loud friends, played in the browser. One container: the game's web page and its server. Open the WebUI, start a crew room, send friends the link.

Config.Name: Web (http)
Config.Description: The game over plain http. Fine on your own network. When PUBLIC_HOST is set, forward the router's port 80 here too (certificates need it).

Config.Name: Web (https)
Config.Description: The game over https. Needed for voice chat and for the public address: forward the router's port 443 here.

Config.Name: Data
Config.Description: Where the https certificates are kept.

Config.Name: PUBLIC_HOST
Config.Description: Your domain name (e.g. yescaptain.duckdns.org). Leave empty until the router forwards 80 and 443 to this container. With it set, the container fetches a real https certificate by itself.

Config.Name: LAN_IP
Config.Description: This server's address on your network (e.g. 192.168.0.6). Switches on https with a self-signed certificate, which the game needs to run at home. Browsers warn once.

Config.Name: HTTPS_PORT
Config.Description: The port https is reached on from outside: the host port above at home, 443 once the router forwards 443 here.

Config.Name: MAX_ROOMS
Config.Description: How many crew rooms may be open at once.

Config.Name: TURN_URL
Config.Description: Optional voice relay (e.g. turn:host:3478) for players whose routers block direct voice.
